shorts.title: What you will learn: std::vector
shorts.hook: The array that grows when you need it.
shorts.script: The array that grows when you need it. Today we meet the most useful container in C plus plus. A vector grows when you add items. A vector is an array that can grow and shrink. Push back adds an item at the end. The size function tells you how many items it holds. A vector looks after its own memory. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: std::vector.

shorts.title: std::vector in one minute
shorts.hook: A vector is an array that can grow and shrink.
shorts.script: A vector is an array that can grow and shrink. Push back adds an item at the end. The size function tells you how many items it holds. A vector looks after its own memory. You never write new or delete. Think of a stretchy shopping bag. It grows when you add more shopping. The vector header gives us the vector type. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: std::vector in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A vector can start with a list of values.
shorts.script: A vector can start with a list of values. Push back adds sixteen at the end. A range-based for visits every item. Back gives the last item, which is sixteen. Pop back removes the last item. Now the size is three. The program prints the four numbers, then sixteen, then three. A vector grows and shrinks. Push back adds an item at the end. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A missing vector header
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The program uses vector, but there is no include line for it. The compiler says vector was not declared in this scope. It suggests the header in a note. Add the include line for vector at the top. The vector type lives in its own header. Without the include line, the compiler has never heard of vector. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
